newsitem.title: UK: NWE gasoline prices retreat after bearish APIs.
newsitem.headline: NWE gasoline prices retreat after bearish APIs.

text.p: NWE gasoline prices went on the retreat on Wednesday sinking $2-3 a tonne after Tuesday's bearish API report showing builds in U.S. oil stocks and a surprisingly bearish decline in demand for gasoline in the U.S., traders said.
Both spot and paper markets were hit with prompt Amsterdam/Rotterdam lifting barges trading some $2-3 lower at $190.50 a tonne and May swaps pegged back $1-2 at $194.75/$195.25.
The API report showed crude stocks up 2.97 million barrels and gasoline up 3.63 million barrels.
Traders said recent reports showing heightened demand for gasoline appeared knocked down by this week's data with demand off some 1.2 million barrels per day from last week's 8.3 million.

However, some said the gasoline build was mainly due to a recent heavy import programme in front of the U.S. driving season and after a recent spell of refinery maintenance. They expected demand to pick up again soon as the U.S. driving season kicks in.
"Gasoline imports have been running nearly double last year, and were eventually going to show-up," Sarah Emerson, director of Energy Security Analysts Inc said.
